## SEO Agent — Content Cadence (v4.3, pipeline rules v4.8)
Runs **once a week in each website's own cycle** (job 6, after the trackers; *Manual Run* `{ trigger: 'cycle', domain, site_id, cycle_key, job, monthly, scheduled_for, request_id }`) and on demand through *Manual Run* (`{ site_id | domain, pages?, dry_run?, force? }`); 48 h before each cycle the dispatcher's `preview` job runs it with `preview: true`: it plans exactly what the cycle would write, writes nothing, and posts stage `cycle_preview` (the "Coming up" plan). For every site with a cadence in `seo_cadence` (set by "Track my site" / API `blogs_per_week`, or Site Admin `cadence`; 1-3 per week) it picks the week's topics in this order: the keyword ladder's next **planned** pages (rung order, with the ladder's internal links), **striking-distance** queries from `seo_query_history` (positions 4-20 with impressions: the page that already ranks gets strengthened), **rising** related searches from `seo_trends`. Keywords written in the last 90 days, written/published ladder pages, brand queries and paused sites are skipped.
Each pick starts a content run in SEO Agent v4 (`mode: keyword`, `force_content`, internal rate-limit key `cadence:<site>`) that delivers the PDF/Word report **plus the blog package** (article HTML, Markdown, meta.json) by e-mail / callback (`stage: content`). The run is logged in `seo_content_log` (status started), ladder rows go to *writing*, and one note per site goes out (`stage: content_cadence`): this week's pages and why, what comes next, pages still waiting for a publish link.
**An AI target says `writing` only while a run is on record, and `written` only when a page is (B9-6, INVARIANTS rule 4).** *AI Target Marks* marks a `seo_ai_targets` row `writing` with the run's id and the plain reason that nothing exists yet; a spawn that **failed** puts the row back to `queued` with its error, so the question is picked again instead of claiming work in progress for ever. *AI Target Settle* is the only exit: a row moves to `written` against a `seo_content_log` row for that same run saying `written` or `published` — R1's rule, in the one table R1 did not cover. A row with no such log row is left alone; AI Growth queues the question again after 14 days with its reason and a medium alert.
**Pipeline rules (v4.8)** from `seo_ladder_settings` (written by the web app; one row per ladder + a `_site` row with the website defaults; no row = the site's default mode or Auto, active, priority by start date): only **Auto** ladders with status active / queued are written, at most `max_active` (default 2) at a time in **priority** order (ladder 1's pages before ladder 2's; plan type *direct* writes the main page first); the **main page waits** until half of the supporting pages are published or the main keyword ranks 1-30; a ladder whose main keyword held the **top 3 for 4 checks** gets no more pages; with `max_waiting` (default 3) pages written but not published the site is **paused** (`paused_reason: pileup`; on demand `force: true` bypasses it); **Manual** ladders' next pages are listed in `awaiting_approval`. Sites without a page but with news get a *Cadence Status* note (same callback stage).
**Keyword-first (2026-10-19, SCHEDULING_KEYWORDS_PLAN.md §5):** the website's `autopilot_level` (`_site` row, 1-3, default 2) decides what runs on its own: 1 = the ladder pages of ladders the client chose (`chosen_by` client_*; `system_announced` only at 3); 2 = also refreshes of the client's existing pages in topic (decay, striking distance with a page, AI refresh); 3 = also new topics (rising trends, AI answer pages on top by `ai_pages_month`). Levels 1-2 write **nothing** before the first chosen ladder ("Waiting for your first keyword"). The fit gate runs on every non-ladder candidate; everything not automatic is a priced **suggestion**. `pages_per_week` bounds everything (0 = nothing), and pages a ladder start or an earlier run of the same cycle wrote count against it (R-K7). The client's skips / approvals come from `seo_skips`. `preview: true` (48 h before a cycle) writes nothing and sends one `cycle_preview` callback (*Cadence Preview*).
The owner publishes in any CMS and reports the URL ("I published a page" in the form, or API `mode: published`): the page is checked live, logged as published, the ladder row gets the real URL, and the Site Tracker inspects indexing and positions from the next Monday. `dry_run: true` only plans. Cost: about $1.20 of AI per page.
